label: thm:epsilon-to-second-difference
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:epsilon-to-second-difference}
  Let $f\colon I\to\mathbb{R}$ be $L$-Lipschitz with $L<1$ and $0<\alpha\leq1$. Suppose that
  \[
    {\widetilde{{\varepsilon}}}_f(z,r)\leq C_{\varepsilon} r^\alpha
  \]
  for some $z\in I$ and $r$ as below. If $h>0$,
  \[
    r :=|{\varphi}_f(z+h)-{\varphi}_f(z)| \quad\text{and}\quad [z-r,z+r]\subset I,
  \]
  then
  \begin{equation}
    |\delta_h^2f(z)|\leq M h^{1+\alpha},\qquad
    M=(1+L)(1+L^2)^{(1+\alpha)/2}C_{\varepsilon}.
  \end{equation}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the choice of $r$, the right intersection point of $\Gamma_f\cap S({\varphi}_f(z),r)$ is $X_+ :={\varphi}_f(z+h)$.
  Write the left one as $X_- :={\varphi}_f(z-k)$, where $k\in (0,r]$, and put
  $X :={\varphi}_f(z)$ and $v_\pm :=X_\pm-X$.

  Let $\theta\in(0,2\pi)$ be the angle of the arc of $\partial B({\varphi}_f(z),r)$ in $\Omega_f^+$. Then
  \[
    {\widetilde{\varepsilon}}_f(z,r)=|\theta-\pi|,
  \]
  and elementary circle geometry gives
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:vector-estimate}
    |v_++v_-|=2r|\cos(\theta/2)|
    =2r\sin\bigl({{\widetilde{\varepsilon}}}_f(z,r)/2\bigr)
    \leq C_{\varepsilon} r^{1+\alpha}.
  \end{equation}

  Recall that
  \[
    v_++v_-=(h-k,\ f(z+h)+f(z-k)-2f(z)).
  \]
  Consequently,
  \begin{align*}
    |\delta_h^2f(z)|
     & \leq |f(z+h)+f(z-k)-2f(z)|+|f(z-h)-f(z-k)| \\
     & \leq |v_++v_-|+L|h-k|                      \\
     & \leq(1+L)|v_++v_-|                         \\
     & \leq(1+L)C_{\varepsilon} r^{1+\alpha}.
  \end{align*}
  Finally,
  \[
    h\leq r=\sqrt{h^2+|f(z+h)-f(z)|^2}\leq\sqrt{1+L^2}\,h,
  \]
  which proves the claim.
head: environment

label: lem:second-difference
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:quotient-step
title: Proof
body_md:
For $t>0$ with $[x,x+t]\subset I$, set
  \[
    q_t^+(x)=\frac{f(x+t)-f(x)}t.
  \]
  The hypothesis, applied at the midpoint of $[x,x+t]$, gives
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:quotient-step}
    |q_t^+(x)-q_{t/2}^+(x)|
    =\frac{|\delta_{t/2}^2f(x+t/2)|}{t}
    \leq\frac{M}{2^{1+\alpha}}t^\alpha.
  \end{equation}
  Fix a compact subinterval $J\subset I$ and choose $t_0>0$ small enough such that $q_{t_0}^+$ is defined on $J$.
  Summing \cref{eq:quotient-step} shows
  that $(q_{2^{-m}t_0}^+)_m$ converges uniformly to a continuous function $v$.

  We now show that $v$ is indeed the derivative.
  For any $a<b$ in the interior of $J$ and $t_m=2^{-m}t_0$,
  \begin{align*}
    \int_a^b q_{t_m}^+(x)\,dx
    =\frac1{t_m}\bigg( \int_b^{b+t_m}f(s)\,\mathrm{d} s - \int_a^{a+t_m}f(s)\,\mathrm{d} s \bigg)
    \longrightarrow f(b)-f(a)
  \end{align*}
  by continuity of $f$. Uniform convergence gives
  $f(b)-f(a)=\int_a^b v(x)\,dx$. Since $v$ is continuous, the fundamental
  theorem of calculus implies $f'=v$. Applying this on compact subintervals
  proves $f\in C^1(I)$.

  Now telescope \cref{eq:quotient-step} starting from any admissible $t$.
  As the quotients converge to $f'(x)$, we obtain
  \begin{equation}
    |f'(x)-q_t^+(x)|
    \leq\frac{M}{2^{1+\alpha}}t^\alpha\sum_{m=0}^\infty2^{-m\alpha}
    =\frac{M}{2(2^\alpha-1)}t^\alpha.
  \end{equation}
  The same argument for backward quotients
  $q_t^-(y)=(f(y)-f(y-t))/t$ gives the identical bound. If $x<y$ and $t=y-x$,
  then
  \[
    q_t^+(x)=\frac{f(y)-f(x)}{y-x}=q_t^-(y).
  \]
  Adding the two bounds proves \cref{eq:holder-constant}.

label: thm:planar-interval
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $J=(-1/4,1/4)$. If $z-h,z+h\in J$ and $h>0$, then $|z|<1/4$ and
  $h<1/4$. Hence,
  \[
    r=|{\varphi}_f(z+h)-{\varphi}_f(z)|\leq\sqrt{1+L^2}\,h<\frac{\sqrt2}{4}.
  \]
  In particular, $[z-r,z+r]\subset(-1,1)$.
  \Cref{thm:epsilon-to-second-difference} therefore gives \cref{eq:criterion-hypothesis} on $J$.
  \Cref{lem:second-difference} now proves the claim.

label: teolipschitz
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{teolipschitz}
  Let $0<\alpha<1$, let $\Gamma\subset{\mathbb R}^{n+1}$ be the Lipschitz graph through the origin of a function $f:{\mathbb R}^n\to{\mathbb R}$ with slope $L\leq \lambda_0$,  for
  some fixed $0<\lambda_0<1/2$ small enough, and let $\Omega$ be one of the connected components of
  ${\mathbb R}^{n+1}\setminus \Gamma$. Suppose that
  $${\varepsilon}_n(x,r) \leq C_{\varepsilon}\,r^\alpha\quad \mbox{ for all $x\in\Gamma\cap B(0,1)$, $0<r\leq1$.}$$
  Then $f\in C^{1,\alpha}(B(0,1/4))$, with
  $$\|\nabla f\|_{\dot C^\alpha(B(0,1/4))} \lesssim C(\alpha,\lambda_0)\,C_{\varepsilon}.$$

label: thm:a-eta-decay
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\rho$ is radial, we have
  \begin{align*}
    a_{\rho,\Omega_g^+}(x,r)
     & = \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \left|  \int_0^{\infty} \psi\Big(\frac{t}{r}\Big) \mathcal{H}^{n}(\Omega_g^+\cap S(x,t)) \,\mathrm{d} t -  \int_0^{\infty} \psi\Big(\frac{t}{r}\Big) \mathcal{H}^{n}(H_x^+\cap S(x,t)) \,\mathrm{d} t  \right| \\
     & \le \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\infty} \left|  \psi\Big(\frac{t}{r}\Big) \right| \left| \mathcal{H}^{n}(\Omega_g^+\cap S(x,t)) - \frac{1}{2}\mathcal{H}^{n}(S(x,t)) \right| \,\mathrm{d} t                                          \\
     & \leq \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\infty} \left|  \psi\Big(\frac{t}{r}\Big) \right| {\widetilde{\varepsilon}}_g(x_0,t) t^n \,\mathrm{d} t                                                                                                        \\
     & \lesssim \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\infty} \left|  \psi\Big(\frac{t}{r}\Big) \right| t^{n+\alpha} \,\mathrm{d} t
    = r^\alpha \int_{0}^{\infty} \left| \psi(s) \right| s^{n+\alpha} \,\mathrm{d} s                                                                                                                = cr^{\alpha}.
  \end{align*}
head: environment

label: thm:LP-equals-a-rho
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $x=\varphi_g(x_0)$ and $K_x=x+K$. By the
  independence of the half-space in the definition of $a_{\eta,\Omega_g^+}$, choose $H_x=\{y:y_{n+1}=g(x_0)\}$ and
  its upper half-space.
  We calculate
  \begin{align*}
    r^{n+1} a_{\eta,\Omega_g^+}(x,r)
     & = \left|  \int_{\Omega_g^+} \eta\Big(\frac{y-x}{r}\Big) \,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(y) -  \int_{H_x^+} \eta\Big(\frac{y-x}{r}\Big) \,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(y) \right|                                                     \\
     & = \left|  \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \psi\bigg(\frac{|y_0-x_0|}{r}\bigg) \left( \int_{g(y_0)}^{F_{K_x}(y_0)} \,\mathrm{d}y_{n+1}  - \int_{g(x_0)}^{F_{K_x}(y_0)} \,\mathrm{d}y_{n+1} \right) \,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{H}^{n}(y_0)  \right|   \\
     & =  \left|  \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \xi\bigg(\frac{y_0-x_0}{r}\bigg) ( g(x_0) - g(y_0)) \,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{H}^{n}(y_0)  \right|                                                                                                      \\
     & =  \left|  \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \xi\bigg(\frac{y_0-x_0}{r}\bigg) g(y_0) \,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{H}^{n}(y_0)  \right|                                                                                        = r^{n} |\xi_r * g(x_0)|,
  \end{align*}
  where $F_{K_x}$ denotes the function corresponding to the cone $x+K$.
  We used that $\int \xi \,\mathrm{d}x_0 = 0$.
head: environment

label: thm:difference-of-a-coeff
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first rewrite $a_\rho(x,r)$:
  Let $K_x^+ := \{ y\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1} : y_{n+1} - x_{n+1} > C_K L |y_0 - x_0| \}$ be the {\em upper opening} of the cone $K_x$.
  If we choose $H_x$ to be contained in the cone $x+K$, we have $K_x^+ \subset \Omega_g^+ \cap H_x^+$, and thus for $x\in \partial \Omega_g^+$ and $r>0$,
  \begin{align*}
    a_{\rho,\Omega_g^+}(x,r) &
    = \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \bigg|  \left( \int_{\Omega_g^+} \rho\Big(\frac{y-x}{r}\Big) \,\mathrm{d} y - \!\int_{K_x^+} \rho\Big(\frac{y-x}{r}\Big) \,\mathrm{d} y \right) \\
                             & \qquad \quad
    - \left( \int_{H_x^+} \rho\Big(\frac{y-x}{r}\Big) \,\mathrm{d} y  -\! \int_{K_x^+} \rho\Big(\frac{y-x}{r}\Big) \,\mathrm{d} y \right)
    \bigg|                                                                                                                                                              \\
                             & = \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \left|  \int_{\Omega_g^+\cap K_x} \rho(\frac{y-x}{r}) \,\mathrm{d} y
    - \int_{H_x^+\cap K_x} \rho(\frac{y-x}{r}) \,\mathrm{d} y
    \right|.
  \end{align*}
  We use this to calculate
  \begin{align*}
     & \left|  a_\eta(x,r) - a_\rho(x,r)  \right|                                                                          \\
     & \le \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \bigg|
    \left( \int_{\Omega_g^+\cap K_x} \psi\bigg(\frac{|y_0-x_0|}{r}\bigg) \,\mathrm{d} y
    - \int_{H_x^+\cap K_x} \psi\bigg(\frac{|y_0-x_0|}{r}\bigg) \,\mathrm{d} y
    \right)                                                                                                                \\
     & \qquad\qquad\qquad -
    \left( \int_{\Omega_g^+\cap K_x} \psi\bigg(\frac{|y-x|}{r}\bigg) \,\mathrm{d} y
    - \int_{H_x^+\cap K_x} \psi\bigg(\frac{|y-x|}{r}\bigg) \,\mathrm{d} y
    \right)
    \bigg|                                                                                                                 \\
     & \le \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_{(\Omega_g^+ \Delta H_x^+) \cap K_x}
    \left|  \psi\bigg(\frac{|y_0-x_0|}{r}\bigg) - \psi\bigg(\frac{|y-x|}{r}\bigg) \right| \,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(y) \\
     & \le \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \sum_{k\ge 0}
    \int_{A_{k,x,r}\cap (\Omega_g^+ \Delta H_x^+) \cap K_x} \lVert \psi' \rVert_{L^{\infty}((2^k - 1, c2^{k+1}))}
    \left|  \frac{|y_0-x_0| - |y-x| }{r}  \right|  \,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(y)                                        \\
  \end{align*}
  where $A_{0,x,r} := B(x_0, 2r)\times \mathbb{R}$ and
  \begin{align*}
    A_{k,x,r} := \{ y \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1} : |y_0 - x_0| \in (2^kr, 2^{k+1}r) \} ,\qquad\forall k\ge 1.
  \end{align*}
  When applying the mean value theorem, note that $y\in A_{k,x,r}$ implies that $|y_0-x_0|/r \in (2^k - 1,2^{k+1})$.
  Since $y\in K_x$, we also have $|y-x|/r \lesssim |y_0-x_0|/r \lesssim 2^{k+1}$,
  and
  \begin{align*}
    \left|  |y_0-x_0| - |y-x|  \right| \le |1-\cos(\arctan C_K L)| |y-x| \lesssim 2^k L^2 r.
  \end{align*}
  Since $\psi$ is a Schwartz function, we have $\lVert \psi' \rVert_{L^{\infty}((2^k - 1, c2^{k+1}))} \le c(M) 2^{-Mk}$ for any $M\in \mathbb{N}$.

  We use affine approximating functions on consecutive dyadic scales to estimate the Hausdorff measure.
  For $j\ge 1$, let $\ell_j$ denote the affine function minimizing $\mathfrak b_g(x_0, 2^jr)$.
  Let $\ell_0 := \ell_1 - \ell_1(x_0) +g(x_0)$ and $H_x$ be the hyperplane associated to it.
  The Lipschitz condition of $g$ at $x_0$ implies that $|\nabla \ell_1| \le 2L$, and indeed $H_x$ is contained in the cone $x+K$:
  \begin{align*}
    2r|\nabla \ell_1|
    \le \lVert \ell_1 - g(x_0) \rVert_{L^{\infty}(B(x_0,2r))}
    \le \lVert \ell_1 - g \rVert_{L^{\infty}(B(x_0,2r))} + \lVert g - g(x_0) \rVert_{L^{\infty}(B(x_0,2r))}
    \le 4Lr.
  \end{align*}
  We have $\lVert \ell_1 - \ell_0 \rVert_{L^{\infty}(B(x_0,2r))} = |\ell_1(x_0) - g(x_0)| \le 2r \mathfrak b_g(x_0,2r)$.
  For $k+1\ge j\ge 2$,
  \begin{align*}
    \lVert \ell_j - \ell_{j-1} \rVert_{L^{\infty}(B(x_0,2^{k+1}r))}
     & \le \frac{2^{k+1}r}{2^{j-1}r}\lVert \ell_j - \ell_{j-1} \rVert_{L^{\infty}(B(x_0,2^{j-1}r))} \\
     & \le 2^{k+1}r ( \mathfrak b_g(x_0,2^{j-1}r) + 2 \mathfrak b_g(x_0,2^{j}r)).
  \end{align*}
  We have
  \begin{align*}
    \mathcal{H}^{n+1}(A_{k,x,r}\cap (\Omega_g^+ \Delta H_x^+))
     & \le \int_{B(x_0, 2^{k+1}r)} |g - \ell_0| \,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{H}^{n}                                                       \\
     & \lesssim (2^{k+1}r)^n \Big\| g - \ell_{k+1} + \sum_{j=1}^{k+1}  (\ell_j - \ell_{j-1}) \Big\|_{L^{\infty}(B(x_0,2^{k+1}r))} \\
     & \lesssim (2^{k+1}r)^{n+1} \sum_{j=1}^{k+1} \mathfrak b_g(x_0,2^jr).
  \end{align*}

  Combining all estimates yields
  \begin{align*}
    \left|  a_{\eta,\Omega_g^+}(x,r) - a_{\rho,\Omega_g^+}(x,r)  \right|
     & \lesssim \frac{L^2}{r^{n+1}} \sum_{k\ge 0} 2^{(1-M)k} \sum_{j=1}^{k+1} \mathfrak b_g(x_0,2^jr) (2^kr)^{n+1} \\
     & \lesssim L^2 \sum_{j\ge 1} \mathfrak b_g(x_0,2^jr) \sum_{k\ge j-1} 2^{(n+2-M)k}                             \\
     & \lesssim L^2 \sum_{j\ge 1} \mathfrak b_g(x_0,2^jr) 2^{-(M-n-2)j},
  \end{align*}
  for sufficiently large $M$.

label: eqbet**1
title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\lVert P_j u  \rVert_{\infty} \lesssim 2^{-j}\lVert u \rVert_{\mathrm{Lip}}$, the estimate follows for $j<0$.

  Now let $j\ge 0$.
  A Taylor expansion of $\chi$ yields
  \begin{align}\label{eqbet**1}
    \left|  P_j u(x_0)  \right|
     & = \left|  \int \xi_{2^{-j}}(x_0 -y_0) \chi(y_0) F(y_0) \,\mathrm{d}y_0  \right|                                                  \\
     & \lesssim  \left|  \int \xi_{2^{-j}}(x_0-y_0)\chi(x_0) F(y_0) \,\mathrm{d}y_0  \right|   \notag                                   \\
     & \quad\quad +
    \left|  \sum_{|\beta| = 1}\int \xi_{2^{-j}}(x_0-y_0) \partial^\beta \chi(x_0)(y_0-x_0)^\beta F(y_0) \,\mathrm{d}y_0  \right| \notag \\
     & \quad\quad + \lVert \nabla^2 \chi \rVert_{\infty} \int |\xi_{2^{-j}}(x_0-y_0)| |y_0-x_0|^2 |F(y_0)| \,\mathrm{d}y_0.\notag
  \end{align}

  For the remainder term we have
  \begin{align*}
    \lVert \nabla^2 \chi \rVert_{\infty} \int |\xi_{2^{-j}}(x_0-y_0)| |x_0-y_0|^2 |F(y_0)| \,\mathrm{d}y_0
     & \lesssim \lVert \nabla^2 \chi \rVert_{\infty} \lVert F \rVert_{\infty} \int |\xi(z_0)||z_0|^2 2^{-2j} \,\mathrm{d} z_0 \\
     & \lesssim 2^{-2j}.
  \end{align*}

  To deal with the term with $|\beta|=1$, using vanishing moments, we write
  \begin{align*}
    \bigg|  \int \xi_{2^{-j}}(x_0-y_0) & \partial^\beta \chi(x_0)(y_0-x_0)^\beta F(y_0) \,\mathrm{d}y_0  \bigg|                                                     \\
                                       & = |\partial^\beta \chi(x_0)| \left|  \int \xi_{2^{-j}}(x_0-y_0) (y_0-x_0)^\beta (F(y_0) - F(x_0)) \,\mathrm{d}y_0  \right| \\
                                       & \lesssim \lVert \nabla \chi \rVert_{\infty} L \int |\xi_{2^{-j}}(x_0-y_0)| |y_0-x_0|^2\,\mathrm{d}y_0
    \lesssim 2^{-2j},
  \end{align*}
  where we can use \cref{eq:f-lipschitz-condition} since $x_0\in\operatorname{supp} \chi$.

  For the term with $\beta=0$:
  Following \cref{thm:lipschitz-at-x0-suffices}, we can apply \cref{thm:LP-beta-estimate} since $F$ satisfies a Lipschitz condition at $x_0\in\operatorname{supp} \chi$.
  Subsequently applying \cref{thm:beta-graph-product} yields
  \begin{align*}
    \chi(x_0) \left|  P_j F(x_0)  \right|
     & \lesssim 2^{-(1+\alpha)j} + L^2 2^{-j} \chi(x_0) \sum_{h\ge 1} 2^{-Nh} \mathfrak{b}_F(x_0, 2^{h-j}) \\
     & \lesssim 2^{-(1+\alpha)j} + L^2 2^{-j} (
    \sum_{h\ge 1} 2^{-Nh} \mathfrak{b}_u(x_0, 2^{h-j}) + \lVert f \rVert_{\infty} 2^{-j} + 2^{-j}
    )                                                                                                      \\
     & \lesssim 2^{-(1+\alpha)j} + L^2 2^{-j} \sum_{h\ge 1} 2^{-Nh} \mathfrak{b}_u(x_0, 2^{h-j}).
  \end{align*}

  Combining all estimates yields the claim.

label: eq:closed-sequence-estimate
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $N>1$.
  Combining \cref{thm:Aj-upper-bound-bk,thm:bk-upper-bound-Aj} gives
  \begin{align}
    A_k
     & \le C_0 2^{-\alpha k}
    +C_1L^2\sum_{h\ge1}2^{-Nh}\mathfrak b_{k-h}
    \notag                                                \\
     & \le C_0 2^{-\alpha k}
    +C_2L^2\sum_{h\ge1}2^{-Nh}
    \sum_{\ell\in\mathbb{Z}}2^{-|k-h-\ell|}A_\ell  \notag \\
     & \le C_0 2^{-\alpha k}
    +C_3L^2\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb{Z}}2^{-|k-\ell|}A_\ell,
    \qquad k\in\mathbb{Z},
    \label{eq:closed-sequence-estimate}
  \end{align}
  since $|k-h-\ell|\ge |k-\ell|-h$.
  Here $C_0$ may depend on $C_\varepsilon$, whereas $C_1,C_2$
  are independent of $L$ and $C_\varepsilon$.

  Since $\alpha<\gamma<1$, we have
  \begin{align}
    \sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}2^{-\gamma|j-k|}2^{-\alpha k}
    \le C_{\alpha,\gamma}2^{-\alpha j}
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    \sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}2^{-\gamma|j-k|}2^{-|k-\ell|}
    \le C_\gamma 2^{-\gamma|j-\ell|},
    \label{eq:weighted-estimates}
  \end{align}
  where the latter follows from the triangle inequality
  in the form
  $\gamma|j-k|+|k-\ell|
    \ge \gamma|j-\ell|+(1-\gamma)|k-\ell|$.

  Set $\gamma=(1+\alpha)/2$ and define
  \[
    \mathcal A_j
    :=\sum_{m\in\mathbb{Z}}2^{-\gamma|j-m|}A_m \lesssim \sum_{m\in\mathbb{Z}} 2^{-\gamma|j-m|} \lVert u \rVert_{\mathrm{Lip}}<\infty.
  \]
  Fix $j\in\mathbb{Z}$. Multiply \cref{eq:closed-sequence-estimate}
  by $2^{-\gamma|j-k|}$ and sum in $k$.
  Interchanging nonnegative sums and applying
  \cref{eq:weighted-estimates}
  gives
  \begin{align*}
    \mathcal A_j
     & \le C_0\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} 2^{-\gamma|j-k|}2^{-\alpha k}
    + C_3L^2\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb{Z}}A_\ell \sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} 2^{-\gamma|j-k|}2^{-|k-\ell|}                      \\
     & \le C_0C_{\alpha,\gamma}2^{-\alpha j}  +  C_3C_\gamma L^2  \sum_{\ell\in\mathbb{Z}}2^{-\gamma|j-\ell|}A_\ell \\
     & = C_0C_{\alpha,\gamma}2^{-\alpha j}  +  C_3C_\gamma L^2\mathcal A_j.
  \end{align*}

  Choosing $\lambda_0$ sufficiently small yields
  \[
    A_j\le\mathcal A_j
    \le 2C_0C_{\alpha,\gamma}2^{-\alpha j},
    \qquad j\in\mathbb{Z}.
  \]
  Consequently,
  \[
    \sup_{j\ge1}2^{(1+\alpha)j}\lVert P_ju \rVert_\infty
    =
    \sup_{j\ge1}2^{\alpha j}A_j
    <\infty.
  \]
  Together with $\lVert S_0u \rVert_\infty<\infty$,
  \cite[Theorem 1.4.9]{grafakosModernFourierAnalysis2014} gives
  $u\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^n)$.
  Since $u=f$ on $B(0,1/4)$, the conclusion follows.

label: mainlemma
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{mainlemma}
  Let $\Omega\subset{\mathbb R}^{n+1}$ be a bounded open set with $n$-Ahlfors regular boundary and let $0<\alpha<1$. Suppose that there exists some constant $C$ such that
  $${\varepsilon}_n(x,r)\leq C\,r^{\alpha}\quad \mbox{ for all $x\in{\partial\Omega}$ and all $0<r\leq {\rm diam}({\partial\Omega})$.}$$
  Then, for $R>0$ small enough and for every $x\in{\partial\Omega}$, ${\partial\Omega}\cap B(x,R)$ is a Lipschitz graph (possibly rotated) with slope at most $\lambda_0$.
head: environment
name: \bf Main Lemma

label: lemreifemberg
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemreifemberg}
  Let $\Omega\subset{\mathbb R}^{n+1}$ be a bounded open set with $n$-Ahlfors regular boundary. Let $x\in{\partial\Omega}$ and $0<r\leq{\rm diam}({\partial\Omega})$.
  For any $\delta>0$, there exist constants $A>1$ and $0<\rho<1$ such that if
  $$\int_0^{Ar}{\varepsilon}_n(y,t)^2\,\frac{dt}t\leq \rho\quad \mbox{ for all $y\in B(x,Ar)$, $0<t\leq Ar$,}$$
  then
  $$\beta_{{\partial\Omega}}(x,r)\leq \delta.$$
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
Let $\Omega$ be a two-sided corkscrew open set with Ahlfors regular boundary. There exists $\epsilon_0>0$ depending on the two-sided corkscrew and Ahlfors regularity conditions such that, for $x\in{\partial\Omega}$, $0<r\leq {\rm diam}({\partial\Omega})$, if $\beta_{{\partial\Omega}}(x,r)\leq \epsilon$ with $\epsilon\leq \epsilon_0$, then
  $$b\beta_{{\partial\Omega}}(x,r/2)\leq C\epsilon.$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $L$ be an $n$-plane passing through $x$ such that ${\rm dist}(y,L)\leq 2\epsilon r$ for all $y\in B(x,r)$. Equivalently, ${\partial\Omega}\cap B(x,r)
    \subset F_L$, where $F_L$ is the closed $(2\epsilon r)$-neighborhood of $L$. We claim one of the components of $B(x,r)\setminus F_L$, which we denote by $V^+$, is
  contained in $\Omega^+$ and the other, which we denote by $V^-$, is contained in $\Omega^-$.

  Indeed, since $V^\pm$ are connected, $V^+$ is contained in
  either $\Omega^+$ or $\Omega^-$, and the same holds for $V^-$.
  By the two-sided corkscrew condition, there exist balls $B^\pm$
  contained in $\Omega^\pm\cap B(x,r)$ with radius $r(B^\pm)\geq c_0 r$. Assuming $2\epsilon\leq c_0/2$, it follows that both balls $B^\pm$ intersect $B(x,r)
    \setminus F_L$. So $V^+\cup V^-$ intersects both $\Omega^+$ and $\Omega^-$. This implies that one component, say $V^+$, is contained in $\Omega^+$, and the other, $V^-$, in $\Omega^-$.

  To see that $b\beta_{\partial\Omega}(x,r/2)\leq C\epsilon$, for a point $x\in L\cap B(x,r/2)$ let $S_x$ be a segment orthogonal to $L$ with length
  $5\epsilon r$, whose mid-point is $x$. Then one of the end-points is contained in $V^+$ and the other in $V^-$. Since $V^\pm\subset
    \Omega^\pm$, there exists a point $z_x\in S_x\cap{\partial\Omega}$. So
  $${\rm dist}(x,{\partial\Omega})\leq \frac12 \,{\mathcal H}^1(S_x) = \frac52\,\epsilon r.$$
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $\Omega\subset{\mathbb R}^{n+1}$ be a bounded open set with $n$-Ahlfors regular boundary and let $0<\alpha<1$. Suppose that there exists some constant $C$ such that
  $${\varepsilon}_n(x,r)\leq C\,r^{\alpha}\quad \mbox{ for all $x\in{\partial\Omega}$ and all $0<r\leq {\rm diam}({\partial\Omega})$.}$$
  Then, for any $\delta>0$, there exists $r_0>0$ depending on $\delta$ such that $b\beta_{{\partial\Omega}}(x,r)\leq \delta$ for all $x\in{\partial\Omega}$ and $0<r\leq r_0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This follows from the previous lemmas, taking into account that $\Omega$ is a two-sided corkscrew domain, by \cite{CTV}.

label: lempju
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lempju}
  For $j\leq k_0$, it holds that
  $$\|P_ju\|_\infty \lesssim \epsilon\,2^{-k_0(n+1)+jn}.$$
  For every $j\geq k_0\geq1$ and $x_0\in L_0$, it holds that
  $$|  P_j u(x_0)|  \lesssim  2^{-2j+k_0} +   \left|\chi(x_0)\int \xi_{2^{-j}}(x_0-y_0) A(y_0) \,\mathrm{d}y_0  \right|.$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $j\leq k_0$, using that $P_ju = \xi_{2^{-j}} * u$, where $*$ is the convolution in ${\mathbb R}^n$, we get
  $$\|P_ju\|_\infty \leq  \|\xi_{2^{-j}}\|_\infty \|u\|_{L^1({\mathbb R}^n)} \leq \frac1{2^{-jn}}\,\epsilon \,2^{-k_0(n+1)}.$$

  On the other hand, for $j\geq k_0$, we argue as in \cref{thm:Aj-upper-bound-bk}, using that $\|\nabla^i\chi\|_\infty\lesssim 1/R_0^i$ for $i=1,2$, and that $\|u\|_\infty \lesssim \epsilon\,2^{-k_0}$, $\|\nabla u\|_\infty \lesssim \lambda_0\leq1$.

label: lembkloop
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We choose $N=1$.
  Then the term on the left-hand side of \cref{eqsumk*} equals
  \begin{align*}
    \sum_{k\geq k_0} \sum_{j\geq k_0} 2^{-|j-k|} \sum_{h<j}2^{-(j-h)} \mathfrak b_{h}
     & \leq \sum_h \mathfrak b_{h} \sum_{j\geq \max(k_0,h)} 2^{-(j-h)} \sum_{k\geq k_0} 2^{-|j-k|} \\
     & \lesssim
    \sum_h \mathfrak b_{h} \sum_{j\geq \max(k_0,h)} 2^{-(j-h)}                                     \\
     & \lesssim
    \sum_h \mathfrak b_{h}  2^{-(\max(k_0,h)-h)} = \sum_h \mathfrak b_{h}  2^{-\max(k_0-h,0)}
    .
  \end{align*}

  We split the last sum as follows:
  $$\sum_h \mathfrak b_{h}  2^{-\max(k_0-h,0)} =
    \sum_{h<k_0} \mathfrak b_{h}   2^{-(k_0-h)} +
    \sum_{k_0\leq h\leq k_1} \mathfrak b_{h}  + \sum_{h>k_1} \mathfrak b_{h} =: T_1+ T_2 + T_3.$$
  To estimate $T_1$ we use the fact that, by \cref{lembkfac}, $\mathfrak b_{h}\lesssim \epsilon$ for all $h\in{\mathbb Z}$, and we deduce that
  $$T_1\lesssim\epsilon.$$
  To deal with $T_3$, we take into account that, by \cref{lembkfac} again, $\mathfrak b_h \lesssim \epsilon 2^{-(h-k_1)}$ for all $h\geq k_1$. This gives
  $$T_3 = \sum_{h>k_1} \mathfrak b_{h} \lesssim \sum_{h>k_1}\epsilon 2^{-(h-k_1)}\lesssim\epsilon.$$
  Gathering the estimates above yields the lemma.

label: lemafc991
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eqavghj34
title: Proof
body_md:
For any $x\in 5B_{Q_0}\cap\Gamma$ and $t>0$, it is easy to check that
  $$\bigl| \mathcal{H}^{n}(\Omega_A^+\cap S(x,t)) - \frac{1}{2}\mathcal{H}^{n}(S(x,t)) \bigr|\lesssim b\beta_\Gamma(x,t)\, t^n.$$
  Then, by the definition of $a_{\rho,\Omega_A^+}$, we get
  \begin{align}
    a_{\rho,\Omega_A^+}(x,r)\label{eqavghj34}
     & = \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \left|  \int_0^{\infty} \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr) \mathcal{H}^{n}(\Omega_A^+\cap S(x,t)) \,\mathrm{d} t -  \int_0^{\infty} \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr) \mathcal{H}^{n}(H_x^+\cap S(x,t)) \,\mathrm{d} t  \right| \notag \\
     & \le \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\infty} \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr) \Bigr| \bigl| \mathcal{H}^{n}(\Omega_A^+\cap S(x,t)) - \frac{1}{2}\mathcal{H}^{n}(S(x,t)) \bigr| \,\mathrm{d} t    \notag                                           \\
     & \lesssim \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\infty} \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr)\Bigr| \, b\beta_\Gamma(x,t)\, t^n \,\mathrm{d} t.
  \end{align}
  From \cref{eqbbetaG1}, it follows that, for $x\in 5B_{Q_0}\cap\Gamma$ and all $r>0$,
  $$ a_{\rho,\Omega_A^+}(x,r)
    \lesssim \epsilon\frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\infty} \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr)\Bigr|\, t^n \,\mathrm{d} t \lesssim \epsilon.
  $$

  For the estimate in (b), we use \cref{eqbbetaG1,eqbbetaG2}:
  \begin{align*}
    a_{\rho,\Omega_A^+}(x,r) & \lesssim
    \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\ell_1} \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr)\Bigr| \, b\beta_\Gamma(x,t)\, t^n \,\mathrm{d} t +
    \frac{1}{r^{n+1}}\int_{\ell_1}^\infty \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr)\Bigr| \, b\beta_\Gamma(x,t)\, t^n \,\mathrm{d} t \\
                             & \lesssim
    \frac{\epsilon}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\ell_1} \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr)\Bigr| \, \frac{t^{n+1}}{\ell_1} \,\mathrm{d} t +
    \frac{\epsilon}{r^{n+1}} \int_{\ell_1}^\infty \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr)\Bigr| \, t^n \,\mathrm{d} t.
  \end{align*}
  For the first integral we write
  $$
    \frac{\epsilon}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\ell_1} \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr)\Bigr| \, \frac{t^{n+1}}{\ell_1} \,\mathrm{d} t
    \leq \frac{\epsilon}{r^{n+1}\ell_1} \int_0^{\infty} \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr)\Bigr| \, t^{n+1} \,\mathrm{d} t
    \approx \epsilon \frac{r}{\ell_1}.
  $$
  For the second integral,
  $$\frac{\epsilon}{r^{n+1}}  \int_{\ell_1}^\infty \Big|\psi\Big(\frac tr\Big)\Big| \,t^{n}\,{\mathrm{d}} t
    \lesssim \frac{\epsilon}{r^{n+1}}  \int_{\ell_1}^\infty \Big(\frac rt\Big)^{n+2} \,t^{n}\,{\mathrm{d}} t
    \approx \epsilon \frac{r}{\ell_1}.
  $$
  Adding the last two estimates, (b) follows.

label: lemmaguai*

label: eqfhjc93
title: Proof
body_md:
For $x$ and $r$ as in the lemma, let $x'\in{\partial\Omega}$ be such that  $|x-x'|\leq \epsilon \ell_1\ll r$, and consequently $x'\in 6B_{Q_0}$. By \cref{lemdifarho},
  \begin{align}\label{eqfhjc93}
    a_{\rho,\Omega_A^+}(x,r) \leq C\epsilon\,\frac{\ell_1}r + a_{\rho,\Omega_A^+}(x',r).
  \end{align}
  As in \cref{eqavghj34}, we have
  \begin{align*}
    a_{\rho,\Omega_A^+}(x',r) &
    \le \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\infty} \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr) \Bigr| \bigl| \mathcal{H}^{n}(\Omega_A^+\cap S(x',t)) - \frac{1}{2}\mathcal{H}^{n}(S(x',t)) \bigr| \,\mathrm{d} t \\
                              & =
    \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \left(\int_0^{\ell_1}\cdots\; +  \int_{\ell_1}^{\ell(Q_0)}\cdots\; + \int_{\ell(Q_0)}^\infty\cdots\right)
    =: I_1 + I_2 +I_3.
  \end{align*}

  For the integral $I_1$ we use \cref{eqbbetaG1} and that $\|\psi\|_\infty\lesssim1$, and then we deduce
  $$I_1\lesssim \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\ell_1} \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr) \Bigr| t^{n-1}\epsilon\ell_1\,\mathrm{d} t
    \lesssim
    \frac{\epsilon}{r^{n+1}} \int_0^{\ell_1}  t^{n}\,\mathrm{d} t\lesssim
    \frac{\epsilon\,\ell_1^{n+1}}{r^{n+1}}.$$
  This follows from the fact that, for $r\leq\ell_1$, $\Gamma\cap S(x',r)$ is contained in a $C\ell_1$-neighborhood of the equator of $S(x',r)$.

  For $I_3$ we use again \cref{eqbbetaG1} and the fact that $|\psi(s)|\lesssim s^{-n-2}$:
  $$I_3\lesssim \frac{1}{r^{n+1}} \int_{\ell(Q_0)}^\infty \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr) \Bigr| t^n\,b\beta(x',t)\,\mathrm{d} t
    \lesssim
    \frac{\epsilon}{r^{n+1}} \int_{\ell(Q_0)}^\infty\Big(\frac{r}{t}\Big)^{n+2}  t^{n}\,\mathrm{d} t\lesssim
    \frac{\epsilon\,r}{\ell(Q_0)}.$$
  To estimate $I_2$ we use \cref{coroguai} to deduce that, for $\ell_1\le t \le\ell(Q_0)$,
  \begin{align*}
    \bigl| \mathcal{H}^{n}(\Omega_A^+\cap S(x',t)) - \frac{1}{2}\mathcal{H}^{n}(S(x',t)) \bigr| &
    \leq \bigl| \mathcal{H}^{n}(\Omega^+\cap S(x',t)) - \frac{1}{2}\mathcal{H}^{n}(S(x',t)) \bigr|                                                   \\
                                                                                                & \quad +
    \mathcal{H}^{n}((\Omega^+ \Delta \Omega_A^+)\cap S(x',t))                                                                                        \\
                                                                                                & \lesssim {\varepsilon}_n(x',t)\,t^n + \epsilon\ell_1 t^{n-1} \\& \lesssim t^{n+\alpha} + \epsilon\ell_1 t^{n-1}.
  \end{align*}
  Therefore,
  $$
    I_2 \lesssim \frac{1}{r^{n+1}}\int_0^\infty
    \Bigl|  \psi\Bigl(\frac{t}{r}\Bigr) \Bigr| \big(t^{n+\alpha} + \epsilon\ell_1 t^{n-1}\big)\,\mathrm{d} t
    \lesssim r^\alpha + \frac{\epsilon\ell_1}r.
  $$

  Gathering the estimates for $I_1$, $I_2$, and $I_3$ and using \cref{eqfhjc93}, the lemma follows.

label: lem7.11
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem7.11}
  We have
  $$\sum_{j\geq k_0} \sup_{x\in 5B_{Q_0}\cap\Gamma} a_{\rho,\Omega_A^+}(x,2^{-j}) \lesssim 2^{-k_0\alpha} + \epsilon.
  $$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We denote
  $$I_1 = \{j:k_0\leq j\leq k_1\},\qquad I_2 = \{j:j> k_1\}.$$

  For the sum over $I_1$ we use \cref{lemmaguai*}.
  Recalling that $\ell_1=2^{-k_1}$, we get
  \begin{align*}
    \sum_{j\in I_1} \sup_{x\in 5B_{Q_0}\cap\Gamma} a_{\rho,\Omega_A^+}(x,2^{-j})
     & \lesssim \sum_{j\in I_1}
    \Big(2^{-j\alpha} + \epsilon\,2^{k_0-j} + \epsilon\,2^{j-k_1} \Big) \\
     & \leq \sum_{j\geq k_0} 2^{-j\alpha}
    +\epsilon \sum_{j\geq k_0} 2^{k_0-j} + \epsilon\sum_{j\leq k_1} 2^{j-k_1} \lesssim 2^{-k_0\alpha} + \epsilon.
  \end{align*}
  To estimate the sum over $I_2$ we use \cref{lemafc991}(b):
  $$\sum_{j\in I_2} \sup_{x\in 5B_{Q_0}\cap\Gamma} a_{\rho,\Omega_A^+}(x,2^{-j})
    \lesssim \sum_{j: 2^{-j}< \ell_1} \epsilon\,\dfrac{2^{-j}}{\ell_1} \lesssim \epsilon.$$
  Adding the two estimates above, the lemma follows.
